well it's it's it's really a tragic story of to be perfectly frank back in twenty fourteen uh... we formed a bipartisan originally without a different name it's is the bipartisan commission on bio it was written blue ribbon panel but to buy right now it's a bipartisan commission on biodefense the co-chairs are tom ridge former first Secretary of Homeland Security and Governor Pennsylvania friend of mine, former Senator Joe Lieberman as the other co-chair, Tom Daschle, former Senate Democratic Leader, Donna Shalala, who was Secretary of HHS in the past and is now a member of Congress and myself and others. With their rheumatoid arthritis drug that's designed to reduce inflammation, one of the phenomenon that was observed in China in the very beginning of this thing was that patients were coming in with these cytokine storms going on in their lungs. that were affecting their lungs because their immune system was over-responding. And so what was happening was the ability of the air sacs and the lungs to transmit oxygen into the capillaries, into the bloodstream. was impeded. And so what they're looking at with this drug is whether they can reduce the inflammation that results from the over-responsive immune system and thereby have patients suffer less from these acute respiratory distress syndrome episodes and lessened. in need of ventilators. The other thing that Regeneron has is this amazing transgenic mice that are designed to have the mimic the human immune response. And so they're giving the injecting the mice with the coronavirus to build antibodies in the mice, which are basically human antibodies because they have a human immune system built into them. And the hope is that while we're waiting for a truly active vaccine, that this might provide a month or two months of vaccine, if you will, prevention protection, at least for the frontline healthcare providers. So those are both pretty exciting possibilities. Everybody's waiting for the remdesivir product that Gilead has to see if it's going to effectively impede the ability of the coronavirus to replicate. The virus has entered the human cells. What they do, of course, is all of the harmers. They're able to replicate themselves. They do that by essentially mining molecules from inside the human cells.
